operationName: Ebola PHEIC Response — 2026 Bundibugyo Outbreak, DRC & Uganda
heroHeadline: BDBV Outbreak: 906 Suspected / 112 Confirmed — WHO Warns 'Catastrophic Collision' of Disease & Conflict
heroSubtitle: WHO's May 27 warning of a 'catastrophic collision of disease and conflict' in eastern DRC came as Mongbwalu — the outbreak's largest cluster with 322 suspected cases and 88 deaths — was disabled by four attack waves, leaving 25+ suspected patients unaccounted and forcing MSF to suspend operations there. WHO Situation Report #2 (May 26) confirmed 906 suspected cases and 223 suspected deaths in DRC, with 112 lab-confirmed total (105 DRC + 7 Uganda). No licensed BDBV vaccine exists; 23% of the outbreak zone remains inaccessible to responders. The situation is now characterized by both a runaway pathogen and an armed conflict actively attacking the response infrastructure.
footerNote: Data sourced from WHO Situation Reports, DRC Ministry of Health (MSANTE), Uganda Ministry of Health, CDC Emergency Operations, MSF field reports, ECDC, US State Department, Oxford University Jenner Institute, and institutional analyses. Case counts and CFR figures are rapidly evolving.
